chunks: From him, from Salih ibn Khalid and Ubays ibn Hasham, from Thabit ibn Sharih, from Dawud al-Abzari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who made a sale but did not have cash on hand, so he went to one of his partners and said, 'Settle the debt for me, and the profit will be shared between you and me.' He replied, 'If it is a profit, it is shared between them both; and if there is a loss, it is upon them both.'
ai.seo_question: How is profit and loss distributed when a partner pays a debt without having cash in a joint venture?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distribution of profit and loss in a *Mudaraba*-like partnership where one partner contributes capital and the other labor, establishing that financial outcomes are shared proportionally unless specified otherwise. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that risk-sharing is intrinsic to valid commercial partnerships, distinguishing it from fixed-fee arrangements. The ruling underscores the fairness inherent in Islamic finance, ensuring that neither party bears the burden of loss alone while enjoying the benefits of gain.
